task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a reported feature of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about the family room that is changing rehearsal arrangements for the Bracken Bell community choir. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Bracken Bell community choir has rented a second room beside its rehearsal hall for parents who bring children to the weekly rehearsal.
Two volunteers organize quiet activities in the side room, while a child's parent or guardian must remain on the premises.
The arrangement is limited to the rehearsal and is not advertised as an independent drop-off childcare service.
The choir pays $25 a week for the extra room during its initial 12-week term, a total room cost of $300.
The room cost is covered by a members' collection, separate from the hall's normal charge for the main rehearsal room.
In the supplied scene, a parent places a music folder beside a bag of crayons before joining the warm-up in the next room.
Choir member Rena Dall said, "I used to do the whole calculation before answering the rehearsal message. This gives me another way to say yes."
The choir does not require a parent to use the side room and still welcomes members who arrange care elsewhere.
The volunteers keep attendance and parent-contact arrangements for the session rather than allowing children to move freely between other hall activities.
Choir director Oren Vell sometimes pauses while a parent responds to a child, then resumes the same passage with the group.
Vell said, "We are adjusting the rehearsal we have, with the people who are actually in it."
Some members asked for a clear boundary between the side-room activities and the quieter parts of rehearsal.
The choir and hall staff agreed which door remains available for family movement and where activities can take place.
The packet does not establish that the arrangement meets every family's needs or guarantees that all interested parents can attend.
The choir has no measured before-and-after membership result for the new room.
The initial plan will be reviewed after the term, including volunteer workload and the cost of retaining the second room.
The hall is also used by a craft club, so the choir packs away the activity materials after each rehearsal.
The side room contains donated books, drawing materials and a washable floor mat rather than new specialist equipment purchased through a large grant.
The choir's repertoire for the term is unchanged by the room arrangement, and no song lyrics are supplied for reproduction.
Adults can join the community choir without audition under its existing membership rules.
The room initiative came from members discussing missed rehearsals, not a citywide survey of childcare demand.
No permanent funding or expansion into sessions outside choir rehearsal has been agreed.

forbidden_additions: An independent drop-off service or guaranteed care for every family.
Measured membership growth, a large equipment grant or permanent funding.
Invented lyrics, private child histories or a claim that the repertoire changed.
preserve: The concrete rehearsal adjustments and members' initiative.
The on-site-parent condition and the limits of the trial arrangement.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
